newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Trial opens of Israeli pig poster suspect.
newsitem.headline: Trial opens of Israeli pig poster suspect.

text.p: The trial opened on Thursday of an Israeli woman accused of putting up posters in Hebron depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig and adjourned for two weeks so she could undergo psychiatric examination.
Tatyana Suskin's defence attorney had asked the Jerusalem District Court to send his 26-year-old client for evaluation to determine whether she is mentally fit to stand trial.

"There is a need to examine the mental state of a person who goes alone into the Palestinian area of Hebron at nine in the evening on a Friday with posters that spark the rage of residents," lawyer Shmuel Caspar told reporters at the court.
The posters, pasted on June 27 across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of the West Bank town, provoked an oupouring of Moslem ire and violent anti-Israeli protests.
Suskin is accused of committing a racist act, harming religious sensitivities, supporting a terrorist group and endangering life by stoning an Arab car. The offences carry a maximum 26-year sentence.
"I regret nothing," she shouted to reporters and called for a Moslem preacher in Hebron "and the rest of the Moslems" to be put on trial for incitement against Jews.
Suskin wore a yellow shirt with the black clenched fist symbol of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane.
